title: CLO Tips Classroom - How to Wrap a Scarf
description: CLO technical expert guides you to quickly create a rolled scarf effect in CLO.
transcript:
This video will explain how to make a rolled scarf in the hollow.  
First, create a new fabric in the object window.  
Then use the lifting plate tool to create a lifting plate measuring 2500x5 mm.  
The thickness of the lifting plate is 25 mm.  
Use the positioning tool in the 3D window.  
Place the lifting plate in front of the scarf.  
Then add a row of fixed needles to the top of the scarf.  
Hold the lifting plate.  
Then select the scarf plate.  
Set the thickness of the lifting plate to 3.  
Set the pressure to 10.  
Use the lifting plate.  
Run the simulation.  
You can see that the scarf automatically rolls up due to the pressure.  
You can hold the lifting plate.  
Press the lifting plate.  
Hold the lifting plate.  
Pull the scarf.  
The scarf will automatically roll up.  
When the scarf is finished, you need to pull it.  
If it is a shorter version, you do not need to pull it manually.  
You can add fixed needles to help adjust the flow.  
Choose all the plates.  
Use the positioning tool to rotate them 90 degrees.  
Then move them to the ground center.  
Choose the scarf plate and move it to the ground center.  
Run the simulation.  
The scarf plate will be neat under the weight.  
Next, improve the quality of the scarf.  
Click to confirm.  
Open the simulation.  
Adjust the shape of the scarf.  
Choose the shape plate.  
Adjust its conflict thickness to 25 mm.  
Organize the package shape of the scarf plate.  
Click to confirm.  
Next, choose the scarf plate.  
Increase the thickness of the scarf to 3 mm.  
Open the simulation.  
Then adjust the conflict thickness to 3 mm.  
After the simulation is even,  
Increase the conflict thickness again to 3.5 mm.  
Open the simulation.  
After the simulation is even, you can delete the shape plate.  
Choose the scarf plate.  
Use the positioning tool to rotate it 90 degrees twice.  
Right-click and place it in the ground center.  
Run the simulation.  
Then delete the fixed needle in the middle.  
After the simulation,  
Right-click to remove hardening.  
Repeat the same process.  
Run the simulation again.  
Next, let's create the stacking effect of three scarves.  
Copy a scarf.  
Move the copied scarf to the ground center.  
Then drag it out with the positioning tool.  
Place it in the correct position.  
Then copy the scarf plate again.  
In the same way, place it on top of the two scarves.  
Adjust its position.  
Place two scarves on top of the two scarves before freezing.  
Then turn on the simulation.  
Make the upper scarf naturally fall on top of the two scarves.  
Freeze.  
Next, enter the enamel window.  
Apply enamel and check the effect of the enamel.  
The enamel effect is the same as the simultaneous enamel effect.  
The above is how we make a scarf in the kiln.  
If you have any questions or other problems, please post them in the comments section.  
Thank you for watching.

chunks.content: # How to Wrap a Scarf Using Fabric Simulation Tools This document explains the step-by-step process to create a rolled scarf effect in a fabric simulation environment using tools such as the lifting plate, fixed needles, positioning tool, and enamel application. It covers technical parameters like dimensions, thickness, pressure settings, and simulation adjustments to achieve realistic scarf wrapping and stacking effects. --- ## Creating the Rolled Scarf Base This section details the initial setup of the fabric and the use of the lifting plate and fixed needles to simulate the automatic rolling of the scarf. - **Create New Fabric:** Start by creating a new fabric object within the software's object window. - **Lifting Plate Setup:** Use the lifting plate tool to create a plate measuring 2500 mm by 5 mm with a thickness of 25 mm. - **Positioning:** Using the positioning tool in the 3D window, place the lifting plate in front of the scarf. - **Fixed Needles:** Add a row of fixed needles along the top edge of the scarf to hold it in place. - **Adjust Parameters:** - Set the lifting plate thickness to 3 mm. - Set the pressure to 10 units. - **Simulation:** Run the simulation to observe the scarf automatically rolling up due to the applied pressure from the lifting plate. - **Manual Interaction:** The scarf can be pulled manually if it is a longer version; shorter versions typically roll up without manual pulling. - **Fixed Needle Adjustment:** Additional fixed needles can be added to help control the flow and wrapping behavior. --- ## Positioning and Aligning the Scarf Plate This section explains how to rotate and position scarf plates correctly for a neat, centered appearance under gravity. - **Select All Plates:** Choose all relevant plates involved in the scarf model. - **Rotate:** Use the positioning tool to rotate the plates 90 degrees. - **Centering:** Move the plates to the ground center in the 3D window. - **Scarf Plate:** Select the scarf plate separately and move it to the ground center. - **Simulation:** Run the simulation to allow the scarf plate to settle neatly under gravity. --- ## Improving Scarf Quality Through Thickness and Shape Adjustments This section focuses on refining the scarf's appearance by adjusting thickness values and conflict thicknesses during simulation. - **Confirm Initial Setup:** Click to confirm the current configuration. - **Open Simulation:** Start the simulation to observe scarf behavior. - **Shape Plate Adjustment:** - Select the shape plate. - Set its conflict thickness to 25 mm. - Organize the package shape of the scarf plate. - **Confirm Changes:** Click to confirm the shape adjustments. - **Scarf Plate Thickness:** - Increase scarf plate thickness to 3 mm. - Open the simulation. - Adjust conflict thickness to 3 mm. - **Final Adjustments:** - After the simulation stabilizes, increase conflict thickness to 3.5 mm. - Run the simulation again until stable. - **Cleanup:** - Delete the shape plate after achieving the desired shape. - Rotate the scarf plate 180 degrees (two 90-degree rotations).

chunks.content: - **Confirm Changes:** Click to confirm the shape adjustments. - **Scarf Plate Thickness:** - Increase scarf plate thickness to 3 mm. - Open the simulation. - Adjust conflict thickness to 3 mm. - **Final Adjustments:** - After the simulation stabilizes, increase conflict thickness to 3.5 mm. - Run the simulation again until stable. - **Cleanup:** - Delete the shape plate after achieving the desired shape. - Rotate the scarf plate 180 degrees (two 90-degree rotations). - Place it in the ground center. - Run the simulation. - Delete the fixed needle in the middle. - Remove hardening from the scarf plate by right-clicking. - Repeat simulation and adjustments as needed. --- ## Creating a Stacked Scarf Effect This section describes how to simulate multiple scarves stacked naturally on top of each other. - **Copy Scarf:** Duplicate the scarf object. - **Positioning:** - Move the copied scarf to the ground center. - Use the positioning tool to drag and place it correctly relative to the first scarf. - **Copy Scarf Plate:** Duplicate the scarf plate. - **Placement:** Place the duplicated scarf plate on top of the two scarves. - **Align:** Adjust the position so that the scarves stack naturally. - **Simulation:** Run the simulation to allow the upper scarf to fall naturally onto the lower two scarves. - **Freeze:** Freeze the simulation once the scarves are settled. --- ## Applying Enamel Effects This brief section outlines the application of enamel finishes to the scarf fabric. - **Open Enamel Window:** Access the enamel settings in the software. - **Apply Enamel:** Apply enamel coating to the scarf. - **Check Effect:** Verify that the enamel effect appears consistent with simultaneous enamel applications. --- # Summary This guide covers the technical steps to simulate a rolled scarf, including fabric creation, lifting plate pressure settings, needle fixes, plate positioning, thickness tuning, and stacking multiple scarves. It also explains how to enhance the final visual quality with enamel application, ensuring a realistic and visually appealing fabric simulation.
